definitions.explanation: The powerful rush of air and pressure generated by an explosion, capable of causing destruction over a wide area.

examples.japanese: {爆風|ばくふう}で{窓|まど}ガラスが{割|わ}れた。
examples.english: The blast shattered the window glass.

examples.japanese: {爆発|ばくはつ}の{爆風|ばくふう}は{数百|すうひゃく}メートル{先|さき}まで{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: The blast wave from the explosion reached several hundred meters away.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}は{爆風|ばくふう}の{影響|えいきょう}で{大|おお}きく{損壊|そんかい}し、{周囲|しゅうい}の{住民|じゅうみん}も{被害|ひがい}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: The building was severely damaged by the blast, and surrounding residents were also affected.

notes:
A compound of {爆|ばく} (explosion) + {風|ふう} (wind). Refers specifically to the destructive wave of compressed air created by an explosion. Common in news coverage of bombings, industrial accidents, and in discussions of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {爆風|ばくふう}で{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばされる: to be blown away by the blast
- {爆風|ばくふう}の{被害|ひがい}: blast damage
- {爆風|ばくふう}の{影響|えいきょう}: effects of the blast
- {爆風|ばくふう}が{届|とど}く: the blast reaches

RELATED TERMS:
- {爆発|ばくはつ}: explosion (the event itself)
- {衝撃波|しょうげきは}: shock wave (more technical/scientific term)
- {爆心地|ばくしんち}: epicenter of an explosion; ground zero
